System UI Nesting Stress Test

Frontend + editor ownership fixture

A — Deep background content

PASS: this paragraph keeps visible internal padding even though it sits inside a Group inside a System Panel.

PASS: this heading also keeps its own background padding.

  • PASS: ordinary background List keeps wrapper padding.
  • FAIL: text touches the colored edge.

B — Structural Row

REVIEW: the Row should not acquire unexplained surface padding merely because it has an editor background.

Primary action
Secondary action

C1 — Panel in Column

PASS: this Panel owns its border, radius, shadow, padding, and nested surface lane.

  • Independent list row one
  • Independent list row two
  • Independent list row three

D — Direct nested System Panel

PASS: this directly nested Panel keeps its own radius and component chrome while consuming the governed nested surface variables.

D1 — Panel inside direct nested Panel

PASS: another authored Panel boundary remains shaped and legible without turning the stack into haze.

E — Deep independent Panel

PASS: two plain Group boundaries do not cause this Panel to lose its radius, border, padding, or surface ownership.

System Details inside independent Panel

REVIEW: the Details component should keep its documented integrated behavior without flattening unrelated descendants.

  • PASS: deep System List row owns its normal surface.
  • PASS: border and radius read as a standalone component.

F — Direct List comparison

The first List is regular; the second is Flush. Their outer geometry should differ intentionally.

  • Direct regular System List
  • Integrated row treatment retained
  • Direct System List Flush
  • Should join the parent shell without duplicate chrome

Review result: mark each section Pass, Fail, or Review.

Fixture complete
